edges.description: The arrested neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor is the lineage within which the two tumour cell identities are defined. The noradrenergic pole carries the committed sympathetic core regulatory circuitry, while the mesenchymal (NCC-like) pole sits close to the undifferentiated neural crest cell, so the two states map onto different points of the same blocked differentiation programme. The evidence cited here locates the two identities in that lineage; it does not show that the arrest itself drives switching between them.

Amplified MYCN raises TERT transcription, which makes MYCN amplification a route to telomerase activation rather than a separate telomere maintenance mechanism. TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours, and in a MYCN-amplified cell line TERT was the gene most strongly downregulated when MYCN was knocked down. Not every MYCN-amplified tumour takes this route: some express TERT as low as ALT tumours do, and forced MYCN overexpression did not induce TERT where the promoter was repressed.
intermediate_mechanisms: Increased TERT transcription driven by amplified MYCN

edges.description: ODC1, the rate-limiting enzyme of polyamine synthesis, is a direct transcriptional target of MYCN, so amplified MYCN raises flux through the pathway. The dependence runs the other way as well, which is what makes the pathway a target rather than only a consequence, but that return relation is recorded in the downstream node's description rather than as a second edge, because an edge back into this node would make a two-node cycle in the pathograph.

Constitutive ALK kinase signalling converges on the same proliferative output as MYCN amplification and co-operates with it; ALK-mutant and MYCN-amplified disease frequently co-occur and jointly enhance malignancy.

Surface GD2 is the antigen the therapeutic antibodies bind, so it is the precondition for antibody-mediated killing. This edge is intervention-conditioned: it carries flux only while an anti-GD2 antibody is being given, and the downstream node describes what the drug then does rather than anything the untreated tumor does.

Telomerase keeps telomeres from eroding, so tumour cells can go on dividing. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither telomerase activity nor ALT showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

Loss of ATRX/DAXX complex function permits alternative lengthening of telomeres. ATRX mutation is associated with loss of nuclear ATRX protein and with ALT, and in one series every ALT tumour carried an ATRX or DAXX alteration. Without ATRX, histone H3.3 is not efficiently deposited at telomeric repeats, replication forks stall there, and the telomeres undergo the homologous recombination that leads to ALT.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of ATRX/DAXX-dependent deposition of histone H3.3 at telomeric repeats

edges.description: ALT maintains telomere length without telomerase, giving the tumour cells that use it an unlimited replicative capacity. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither ALT nor telomerase activity showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.

The state switch is what produces the resistant fraction: cells at or moving towards the mesenchymal pole survive induction chemotherapy, so the mesenchymal proportion rises after treatment. The patient data behind this edge are observational and do not separate therapy-induced switching into the mesenchymal state from survival of mesenchymal cells already present.

Occupying the mesenchymal pole leaves the cells without ALK expression, and so without the drug target, which is why the escape follows from the cell state rather than from any change in ALK itself. Demonstrated in cell lines and in xenografts of those cells.
edges.target: ALK-Inhibitor Escape by Loss of Target Expression

edges.description: The state that confers chemotherapy resistance and ALK-inhibitor escape carries the opposite immune phenotype: the immune-enriched subset of neuroblastomas is the one characterised by mesenchymal lineage signatures, and mesenchymal-state cells are the ones cytotoxic lymphocytes recruit to and kill.

Supplies a molecular switch for the arrest this node asserts: multi-site phosphorylation of Ascl1 converts it from a driver of sympathoadrenal differentiation into an inert factor, matching the phospho-state Ascl1 is held in within neuroblastoma cells.
edges.limitations: Frog AVNA cells are a developmental counterpart of the presumed cell of origin, not tumour cells, and the model contains no transformed tissue — arrest is scored as failure to differentiate on schedule rather than as tumour formation. The link to human disease rests on the observed phospho-state of ASCL1 in neuroblastoma lines, so the model shows the state is sufficient to block differentiation, not that it is what maintains any patient's tumour.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

edges.description: Positions MYCN upstream of the differentiation block: MYCN overexpression prevents Ascl1-driven differentiation, and loses that ability when Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated.
edges.limitations: This is the differentiation-blocking arm of MYCN only. The node is about proliferation, and no proliferative or tumour-growth readout was taken here; MYCN is introduced by overexpression in a normal embryo, not by the genomic amplification that defines high-risk neuroblastoma.
edges.source: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model

nodes.description: ALK tyrosine kinase inhibition targets the constitutive ALK signalling produced by activating ALK point mutations or ALK amplification. The first-generation inhibitor crizotinib has limited activity against several common neuroblastoma ALK variants (notably F1174L), which motivated the move to third-generation, CNS-penetrant inhibitors; lorlatinib is under evaluation in frontline cooperative-group trials for ALK-altered high-risk disease. Applicable only to the ALK-altered molecular subset.

nodes.description: Mesenchymal-type neuroblastoma cells express neither mutant nor wild-type ALK, so ALK inhibition has no target in them and the escape is absence of the drug target rather than an alteration in it. The mesenchymal cells resemble immature precursor cells, which also lack ALK expression, so the absence tracks the identity state the cells occupy. This is a cell-line and xenograft result: the cells were resistant to ALK inhibitors in culture, and tumours formed from them progressed under ALK inhibitor given to the xenografted animals. No patient-level evidence is curated here.

nodes.description:
Neuroblastoma tumour cells occupy two transcriptionally divergent identity states, and the field names them twice over. van Groningen and colleagues name them adrenergic and mesenchymal, defined by a super-enhancer contrast between isogenic cell-line pairs. Boeva and colleagues, profiling the super-enhancer landscape of neuroblastoma cell lines, name a sympathetic noradrenergic identity whose core regulatory circuitry module includes PHOX2B, HAND2 and GATA3, an NCC-like identity driven by a circuitry module containing AP-1 transcription factors, and a mixed type. Mesenchymal and NCC-like are close but not identical concepts: the first is defined by an isogenic-pair super-enhancer contrast, the second by membership of a core regulatory circuitry.
In cell lines and xenografts the switch between the two identities arises spontaneously, runs in both directions and is accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming. The noradrenergic-to-mesenchymal shift occurs in culture; the reverse shift was documented after engraftment in mice. Enforced expression of a NOTCH3 intracellular domain drives the adrenergic-to-mesenchymal direction with genome-wide remodelling of the H3K27ac landscape, and a NOTCH feed-forward loop then maintains the induced state. SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling ATPases are required to establish the mesenchymal gene-permissive chromatin state that facilitates this plasticity.
In patient tumours the dominant identity is noradrenergic. Gene-expression signatures derived from established cell lines fail to identify mesenchymal tumour cells in patient tumours, whereas signatures developed from early-passage orthotopic patient-derived xenografts enable their identification. A minority subpopulation of noradrenergic tumour cells co-expresses mesenchymal features, found in a subset of tumours rather than in all of them, and the mesenchymal-like programme detectable in some pre-treated high-risk patient tumours is weakly expressed, sits inside cancer cells that remain otherwise adrenergic, and appears distinct from the presumptive drug-resistance mesenchymal programmes of cell lines. Whether patient tumours also carry a discrete, purely mesenchymal tumour-cell population of the kind cultured cells show is unsettled; the evidence collected here establishes neither its presence nor its exclusion.
Microenvironmental influence is not one-directional, and the two documented cues were measured in different systems. In mouse xenografts, cells of either starting identity gave rise to tumours with a noradrenergic phenotype, which the authors read as microenvironmental pressure towards that state. In cultured cell panels, hypoxia shifted adrenergic cells towards mesenchymal gene expression.
The mesenchymal state is not the less malignant of the two: in vivo reprogramming of adrenergic cells found mesenchymal and adrenergic cells equally oncogenic.

biological_processes: reversible switching between two tumour cell identities
chromatin remodelling accompanying the identity switch
cell_types: neural crest cell-like (mesenchymal) tumour cell state

nodes.description: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), the recombination-based telomere maintenance mechanism that works without telomerase. Its measured frequency depends on cohort and assay: C-circle screening classified 9.2% of a 720-tumour screening cohort as ALT-positive, ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies marked 49 of 273 pretreatment neuroblastomas, and the C-circle assay marked 25 of 107 high-risk tumours from patients older than 18 months. In a registry cohort of 40 relapsed tumours, 47.5% were ALT-positive. ATRX alterations are found in only about half to 60% of ALT tumours. In primary tumours, ALT and the routes to telomerase activation occur almost mutually exclusively, and ATRX mutation and MYCN amplification co-occurred in only 1 of 819 tumours. ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate slowly, with a protracted clinical course, yet children with these tumours have a dismal outcome. About a third of ALT-positive tumours present with localized disease classified as low or intermediate risk, and in one cohort survival did not differ between ALT-positive tumours classified high risk and those classified low or intermediate risk.

nodes.description: An anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody added to post-consolidation therapy is standard of care in high-risk neuroblastoma. In the randomized COG trial ANBL0032 the comparator arm was isotretinoin, which both arms received, and adding the antibody with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2 improved both event-free and overall survival; the five-year follow-up kept both differences. Dinutuximab is the licensed agent in the United States and dinutuximab beta in Europe. The contribution of the two cytokines is not settled in the way the antibody's is: in the European HR-NBL1/SIOPEN randomization, adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta gave no event-free survival benefit and added toxicity, and the trialists recommended the regimen without it as the standard of care, while the United States label still lists interleukin-2. No trial has ever isolated GM-CSF's own contribution. The benefit is therefore recorded here as a regimen-level effect of anti-GD2-based immunotherapy rather than as an effect of any one component. Grade 3 to 5 pain occurred in about half the immunotherapy arm of ANBL0032, an on-target toxicity of GD2 on peripheral nerves.

nodes.description: An oral ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor given as maintenance after front-line therapy, to reduce the risk of relapse rather than to treat active disease. The United States approved indication, granted on 13 December 2023, is for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy; dosing in the pivotal study was oral, twice daily and continued for up to two years. The evidence base is unusual and the record is written around that: approval rested on an externally controlled trial, a single-arm study compared with an external control drawn from a separate cooperative-group trial, and the review describes it as the first oncology approval to rely on that design as its primary clinical data. Against the external control, event-free and overall survival both favoured eflornithine. No randomized trial has tested it in this setting.

evidence.snippet: On December 13, 2023, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved eflornithine (IWILFIN, US WorldMeds) to reduce the risk of relapse in adult and pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy.

nodes.description: The disialoganglioside GD2 is expressed on the surface of nearly all neuroblastoma cells and only sparsely on normal tissue, which is what makes it the target of antibody therapy. Expression is not uniform, and it can be absent: in a series of 474 patients with unequivocal bone marrow infiltration, tumor cells showed complete or partial negative GD2 staining in 12.0% across diagnosis, treatment and recurrence, and 21 cases converted from positive to negative. nodes.description: Mesenchymal-state cells survive cytotoxic chemotherapy that kills adrenergic cells, and mesenchymal features have been reported to become enriched after chemotherapy and at relapse while adrenergic traits predominate in untreated tumours. What makes this a consequence of plasticity rather than an independent resistance mechanism is that blocking the switch itself prevents the resistance: degrading the SWI/SNF ATPases that hold mesenchymal genes in a permissive chromatin state inhibits plasticity and, with it, the outgrowth of the resistant fraction. The post-treatment enrichment reports are associations and do not separate selection of already resistant cells from therapy-induced switching, and the identity of the mesenchymal programme detectable in patients is not settled, which is why the node is held provisional.

nodes.description: The subset of neuroblastomas enriched for immune-related transcripts is predominantly characterised by mesenchymal lineage gene-expression signatures, while tumours expressing adrenergic lineage signatures are less immunogenic by the same measures. The enrichment covers transcripts of immune activation and of immune inhibition together, so this is not a claim of net anti-tumour immunity: the same tumours carry higher immune-evasion scores. Functionally, mesenchymal lineage cells secrete inflammatory cytokines that recruit T cells and are efficiently killed by cytotoxic T and natural killer cells in culture, and in an immunocompetent mouse model the mesenchymal-marker-enriched, MHC class I-high tumours responded better to combined PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade than their counterparts. The patient-level half is correlative transcriptomics; the killing and checkpoint results are functional and come from cultured cells and from mice.

nodes.description: Neuroblastoma cells raise flux through polyamine biosynthesis, with ODC1 as the rate-limiting enzyme and a direct transcriptional target of MYCN. Elevated ODC1 tracks reduced survival independently of MYCN status in two patient cohorts. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the step from this pathway to the clinical effect of the approved drug is not established: at the approved low dose, polyamine depletion has not been shown to be the operative mechanism, and sensitivity to the inhibitor does not track MYCN or ODC1 copy number. nodes.description: Reduced abundance of the ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodelling complex, a recurrent molecular feature of alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) in neuroblastoma. ATRX encodes an ATP-dependent helicase of the SWI/SNF family of chromatin remodellers and, with DAXX, deposits the histone variant H3.3 at telomeric regions. ALT-positive neuroblastomas show reduced ATRX/DAXX complex abundance, due either to ATRX mutation (55% of them in one cohort) or to low protein expression, while mutations in the complex members DAXX and H3F3A were extremely rare. In a pooled analysis of published ATRX-altered neuroblastomas, 68% of ATRX aberrations were multi-exon deletions, and 75% of these were predicted to be in-frame. ATRX mutation is strongly age-dependent: in 104 patients with metastatic disease, sampled to represent each age group, it was found in tumours from 14 of 32 adolescents and young adults, 9 of 54 children and none of 18 infants, although infant cases are reported. In the pooled analysis, each of the three types of ATRX aberration was more frequent in patients diagnosed at an older age, yet about 40% of the ATRX-aberrant patients were five years or younger at diagnosis.

nodes.description: Telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance, one of the two telomere maintenance mechanisms in neuroblastoma. TERT rearrangements at 5p15.33 juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, with chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region, and despite their structural diversity they all induced massive transcriptional upregulation of TERT. MYCN amplification raises TERT transcription, and some tumours have high TERT expression with neither alteration. In 457 pretreatment neuroblastomas, TERT rearrangement was found in 46 and MYCN amplification in 93, and high TERT expression without either in 10 of 223 tumours with expression data. TERT promoter mutations are rare: none was found in 131 primary tumours representing the whole spectrum of the disease, and a single-centre series found them in 17 of 603 tumours. Activated telomerase, defined by these routes, was associated with the poorest overall survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses. Enzymatic telomerase activity has been shown in neuroblastoma cell lines that carry a TERT rearrangement or MYCN amplification.

nodes.description: The ability of tumour cells to keep dividing indefinitely, which a telomere maintenance mechanism (telomerase activation or ALT) provides. Its binding, increased cell population proliferation, follows the module node it conforms to and means expansion continuing past the limit that telomere shortening sets on normal cells, not a faster division rate: ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate more slowly than telomerase-activated ones. Aggressive neuroblastomas show a prolonged evolution during which they acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms, whereas tumours with a favourable prognosis expand clonally after a short evolution. In pretreatment neuroblastomas, patients whose tumours lacked a telomere maintenance mechanism had an excellent prognosis and those whose tumours had one did substantially worse. Within high-risk disease the picture is less clear: in one cohort the telomere maintenance groups differed in overall but not in event-free survival, and a subset of high-risk tumours lacks significant telomere lengthening activity, with cells derived from them proliferating for more than 200 population doublings while their telomeres shortened.

nodes.description: Rather than growing a tumour, this model reconstructs the normal differentiation of the neural-crest-derived sympathoadrenal cell that neuroblastoma is thought to arise from, and asks what stops it. Frog AVNA cells differentiate under transient Ascl1 expression; in neuroblastoma cells Ascl1 is instead persistently expressed and multiply phosphorylated. Introducing that phospho-state into the frog cells blocks their differentiation, and CDK or MYCN overexpression blocks it too — but not when Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated, which places phosphorylation downstream of both. The model tests the differentiation-arrest hypothesis in a normal developmental context; it does not produce tumours and so says nothing about transformation, growth, or metastasis.
